reviews.text: A fun game where I felt like a sky pirate and found a lot of treasure. And this game runs great even on my weak laptop.
警告：商店页面没标Roguelite，但本作是含有大量局外成长的Roguelite战旗。在一回合只能走两步的操作空间下，敌人还会故意给你留解法，策略难度属于“这不显得您聪明吗”水平

First Impressions: Love the art and atmosphere. Just my cup of tea. Big fan of tactical roguelikes/lites and so far the combat aspect of the game is OK. Its definitely more in the vein of Fights in Tight Spaces or Into the Breach than FF tactics. This game has the problem where you can load into a battle and essentially lose on the spot due to luck. Youll be surrounded by items or creatures with no way out and you start out with very limited action points so you have little agency to change the outcome if you have a bad start. This is mitigated by the fact that you get 1 restart a level that changes the layout and your spawn point but if you get unlucky twice then your run is straight up done. Edit: After learning the game a bit more and reaching the final boss, my previous critique may have just been a skill issue. Overall the game is a solid 7/10. Worth the price, youll get your money's worth and if you like tactical roguelite's sprinkled with a bit of cosmic horror then you'll like this game. The combat becomes more interesting as your character levels up but it also becomes a bit easy. The resource management becomes more of a minor annoyance than something to truly manage once you get some meta unlocks. The enemy variety is honestly pretty good once you've beat the first boss once. Before your first kill of the first boss, its just the same 4 goblins ad nauseum but you really shouldnt be spending that much time on the first act anyway. Again, I think this game is pretty nice, I'd definitely recommend for TBT enjoyers.
Really good tactical game. I was enjoyed turn-based combat. This game is worth the money. Thanks devs.

Pretty good art, solid combat with some interesting aspects. Game feels good and like the devs actually cared about making it. For the price, it's really good. Does however REALLY need controller support. It's kinda ass to try and play on deck. Put some more time into it and for sub $10 this game is great. Combats rewarding when you just accept the madness and embrace the yeeting of enemies into the abyss. Resource management is light and besides boss fights I think they could bump difficulty up a bit for normal enemies. I've started just running the main character until act 3 now and skipping lower mercs.
I spent 1 hour pushing enemies around and still can't figure out if I'm the dead weight or my crew is
太普通了，一点不惊艳，重复的体验也很多，但是游戏不贵。

I played this during Steam Next Fest and had a lo of fun with it. It's a tight little rougelike TRPG desinged for quick bouts. The tutorial is fast and mostly just tect boxes during normal play so it's very unintrusive. This is one of those games that respects your time. You jump right in and there are speed up options and text skips abound for those that just want to jump right in. It won't set the world on fire but it's fun and it's a very cheap buy. The combat and gameplay isn't terribly deep but it's enough to keep you enguaged and the sound and art style work very well.
难度偏低，游戏性还可以 不过属于那种打完了就没什么好玩的了的类型，四个角色应该可以玩三天吧。（那个亚索真的很好玩

It's very good. It's a rougelite with Xcom/Into the Breach style combat, as well as an rpg since you gear-up and level-up your hero. You fly your ship around to pick fights with pirates, though tbh that aspect of the game becomes trivial after a few meta-upgrades. I've only played a couple of the heroes, but their styles are very different, and their capabilities morph considerably throughout the runs. Only real complaint I have is that fights can get cluttered. It takes awhile to figure out which enemy is doing what attack when they all overlap on the same few tiles. But I did get used to it after awhile. Also, idk what is up with the cover art, but it does not match the vibe of this game lol. It's definitely more darker/serious. Not that it really matters, the story is not too involved, nor is there much in the way of dialogue.

I think a meta progression upgrade that gives you faster exp would be good here. I unlocked most of the really useful upgrades, fuel and fatigue are not a problem anymore, but farming 100 pirate ships to reach level 20 is a bit annoying lol

玩不爽，折磨人，开局就三滴血那些怪全部都是2-3攻击能一下秒我，每次只能走两步路，打一个小怪都要花费许多脑子走位卡地下，如果是前期折磨一下后期起来那还可以玩，但是没有后期，主角只能做10个任务，10个任务就掉入深渊重新打，这一把存的那些宝石，金币装备全部消失直接重开，而且死了，飞船燃料没了什么的全部重开直接就是折磨人。 复活一次就给10金币，随便一个烂装备就要我50金币而且居然不加攻击，甚至有些武器还没有技能也没有伤害，一次只能装备一把武器，两个盔甲，消耗品一次只能带两个，那盟友垃圾的也要3-40块钱，好的要100多，也就2滴血，死了你的装备全没了。 每次重开要重新赚钱，金币可以买燃料，买装备，买耐力虽然买的很少但是都很贵，每次出门都要算好距离和燃料，燃料不够回家只能重开，燃料够了但是耐力不够了看着BOSS就在自己面前打不了重开，好不容易摸到BOSS然后进去我一个打7个怪直接没了重开。 1个小时我重开了26把才把第一个BOSS磨死，然后又重开了，我没打过重开，打过了还重开我玩密码的玩，我耍了30分钟的钱耍了400块就想打完BOSS爽，结果直接给我重开去打第二个BOSS但是我的装备金币全没了。

Art is awesome, combat...has potential. but this game is incredibly inconsistent with giving information ans user interface. This skill consumes action point, but this one doesn't. Is it stated anywhere? no. This barrel has durability 1 so when i damage it...it breaks. This piece of ice has durability 1 so when i damage it...nothing happens?? two items are for accessory slot. one has "consumable" in its description, the other doesn't, yet both are consumed upon use. what the hell devs? "shoots over obstacles" yet it cannot shoot over this pitfall...but next turn when i move it CAN shoot over a different pitfall?? and this crap is all over the place. Oh, there is a blue square with an arrow on the battlefield...what does it do? i have no idea, no matter how much i tried to click on it or hover and search for some popup with info...no result. and after stepping on it you know what it does? nothing. or something that i didn't even notice. In highly tactical games such as this one tries to be its INCREDIBLY IMPORTANT to give player all information as clearly as possible and as consistently as possible. When you have to blindly do stuff to explore what it does thats just crappy design for this genre. Especially when it behaves differently every time oh my god. Devs, its not that hard to make everything consistent, i see you really tried to make a good game, but this is the worst ux i had playing strategy games ever. EDIT: I see you're trying to fix things. I dont want to discourage small studios from making new games and ruining releases so Im changing this review to positive. I will be waiting for new update that fixes these problems and would like to try this game again. Good luck.
Really loved the idea of the game! Will play it again n again. I really loved the steampunk thematic!! :)

This game takes a familiar concept and adds a little flair with overworld map exploring and an interesting story. I've only begun to get in the depths of this game but for a $10 game, I am HIGHLY impressed. Are their issues? Yep. Do they break the game? No. There needs to be better descriptions and detail put into some items and some mechanics, (however you can learn what they do by science). The only TRUE gripe I have is there is no controller support. I WANT TO PLAY THIS WITH MY CONTROLLER TO MY TV LET ME LIVE MY LIFE!! Other than that, highly recommend as a $10 gem. The early parts of the game are somewhat stale, it opens up quite a bit as you get to tougher enemies. PLEASE LET ME PLAY ON CONTROLLER PLEASE

this might be the only time I've refunded a game I could actually play. The combat is absolutely terrible and unenjoyable. Half of your run will be spent moving out of the way attacks rather than playing the game. if you're being efficient, most turns you wont even attack.

游戏卖的不贵也没那么差劲，只是比较平庸罢了。一共三个区域，4个可选角色。主要是像素画很好看。由于局外要分每个人物升级来解锁而且要的经验也很多所以重复劳动就很多了，只有一开始有意思后面都是很无聊的重复劳动，地图随机事件只有：休整，拿资源，拿装备，打怪这几种。船的升级属性也只是消耗品。特色也只有把人推到地图外面秒杀，还有躲开敌人的红圈。而且游戏剧情貌似要打个三四遍以上才能看全，我打了一遍就玩不下去了。我觉得这游戏做线性更好些，SRPG和rouguel还是不合适。

问题很严重，战斗系统收益完全不匹配难度，石头强化装备有些根本就是直接把装备原本的词条给砸烂了 雇佣单位性能太差以至于你不给他带个移动力+1根本没法用 主角也是基本上绑着+1移动力和经验衣服 远程攻击单格陷阱全是2伤，导致锁路一格移动力根本跑不了 还有更加逆天的bug，1区小怪有如果有两个扔手雷的眩晕就会无限循环眩晕直接控到死 2区也是，2区有个小怪的远程投掷2血也是打中就无限眩晕到死，我真cnm了什么年代了还能单小怪硬控到死的，不会加入眩晕一次后后续1回合免疫眩晕吗我真cnm了

Cool, so I managed to finish a run after a few tries on the first 3 characters and here are my thoughts after having done so 1. Gameplay : very Into the breach coded, lot of focus on positioning and setting up combos between a crew of 3 dudes with 2-ish actions each. simple setup, but the game does a good job of keeping the level designs interesting and the enemies varied enough to pose a threat. 2. heroes and mercs : each hero character feels unique and has there own gimmick to them that you can play around with. The leveling system kicks all kinds of ass here and grants ur lil guy a lot of unique tools. The mercenaries aint to bad either because theres several different types of varying power lvls, then once you add in the equip system and u can deck out both your hereos and mercs in a hundred different ways to pull off a lot of different styles. 10/10 here. 3. Design: musics solid, arts polished, and the eldritch/steampunsk asthetic is so fun to see. 4. meta progression: this is my jam right here, forces you to play around with different characters so you dont get stuck in a rut, gives a lot of options and the choice in what to prioritize, lets you risk madness in run to push meta progression further, love to see it, no notes. 10/10 game, would fall into the abyss again shadow dashing.

Perhaps this game gets better after much progression, but at least for the first few hours it is a repetitive slog, with annoying mechanics. Annoying mechanic #1: fuel. You burn fuel when moving between encounters, and when you inevitably run out of fuel, which always feels extremely premature, your run is over. There is apparently a gas station unlockable, but even after several hours of play, I never found it. Annoying mechanic #2: after ten encounters, your run is ended. Perhaps this is done for balance reasons, but it just feels annoying. Normally with rogue-lites your run is ended because you progressed to some combat that you couldn't win. But in Dead Weight, your run is ended just because you filled up this arbitrary progress bar. Annoying mechanic #3: the combat is akin to the Breach, which is fine, but it is more simplistic, and extremely repetitive. Due to Annoying Mechanics Numbers 1 & 2, everything is very slow to unlock, which adds further to the repetitiveness. If these annoying mechanics were removed or overhauled, there may be a good game in there.

美术是有点东西的，你给我看大奶我就给你好评。 难度属于老滚式解密，会让人玩家觉得自己很聪明的游戏，在知道可以飞回来歇息后其实也就没什么难度了，通关过一次就不太想玩第二次，内容过于重复。 装备系统这块可以说是非常糟糕，类型不多，而装备进化这一块，除了武器强化就是加数值，其他品质装备好坏没有什么关联，高品质的装备甚至会更弱。 只有2点移动力，行动和移动都会消耗移动点，这个设计初玩觉得还行，玩多了就会觉得攻击频率过少会过于憋屈，但天赋设计又弥补了这一点，会有AOE和回血。
噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢噢~~~（掉下去了）
通关一次就没玩的欲望了，首先像素美术是我的菜而且很精致；但明显本游戏没像做大，地图和bd以及机制都很渺小和无聊； 本以为会像《陷阵之志》有决策深度，但就是走一格等CD；总之玩个10H就腻了，没啥重玩价值，第三个DZ刺客不需要什么装备秒完了，但是所有的装备和成型在机制boss身上发挥不到什么用。及格小游戏，可以用来打发时间等待自己的愿望game
美术风格很赞！就是重复性有点高，目前内容太少了，算是未来可期。那个剑圣真的好玩，好几次都是眼花了冲下岛死了。

用阿恩第三把终于通关了，这一把可能花了我将近4-5个小时。 探索：建议新增一些特殊岛屿，有一些特殊boss，对应特殊奖励，这样可以降低探图的重复度。 boss：三个boss的设计我认为都很有特色，不过找对方法都不算难。想吐槽一下的是最后克拉肯，打之前完全不知道是一个推人机制怪，导致没法提前装备合适的武器做对策，重试时也没有重新配置队伍的选项（加上重试可能花了我一个半小时终于干掉）。可能如果组远攻build会更有选择一些，但我阿恩+奶妈+壮汉打起来还是比较吃力。 后期如果能持续完善，增加更多的boss，更多的随机事件，随机探索，甚至不一样的机制，我认为会是一个挺小而美的rouguelike
肉鸽战棋，有推图运营空间，有碰撞机制和地形秒杀，有大量局外成长。关卡数量和敌人种类太少，每个英雄可选打法也不多，重玩价值不高

[h1][b]致死负重：破浪陷阵，决胜之志，明牌博弈仍需精算的战棋推演[/b][/h1] [hr][/hr] 独立工作室Klukva Games在7月16日释出的《Dead Weight》无疑是《陷阵之志》这类略微硬核小棋盘回合制游戏的同类续作，同时又因为局外的rougelike要素而将无谓的难度削去，玩家只需要在一个[b]满是飞艇哥布林、克苏鲁古神的蒸汽朋克废土[/b]之上完成一盘盘敌意明牌的反击，体会到[b]纯粹的战术致胜，[/b]因为每一局都不容易，[b]负重前行的预判取胜后，更能获得纯粹的智性快感。[/b] Dead Weight的词义外延，恰恰表明了这个游戏的两大特质：战术侧的[b]难移千钧[/b]，以及经营侧的[b]资不抵债[/b]，也正因在这硬核的筹算中，我们必须成为轻盈而精准的手术刀，利用各类机制来[b]完成一关多解[/b]。 [h2][b]寡能敌重：战术策略游戏最核心的魅力永远是思考的乐趣[/b][/h2] 本作并不打算用巨大的地图来营造史诗感，战场往往只是几层狭小的飞艇甲板或微型悬浮岛，我们将扮演四位英雄，在古神的召引下，清理秽悒的异徒，或许会重坠深渊，但当我们带着Meta进度杀出冥界的时候，自身的强化会给战场带来更多新的解法。 游戏中每一场战斗都是随机的出题（点击左下角的重开，[b]障碍物以及怪物的出生点都会变位[/b]），在加上怪物强制先动给玩家带来的移动阻碍，让角色无法依靠数值碾压，而是必须在走位中完成[b]小刀割肉地减员[/b]。 每一个回合，敌人的攻击意图、落点和伤害都是已知的出题信息，[b]100%确定的明牌博弈、主控角色有限的行动点以及微缩棋盘中以多打少的步步紧逼[/b]，开战即决战，我们必须置死地而生急智。 [list] [*]强力的武器绝非冷热兵器，而是[b]位移（某一个英雄的被动技能就是依靠不断的移动，才能打出可观的伤害）[/b]，由于敌人的意图是上了发条无法临场更改的，所以轻巧地走出攻击范围是减少战损的第一步 [*]位移带来的连锁便是，怪物在玩家回合后的移动会被我们诱敌，而游戏中[b]存在友伤[/b]，因此适当剌开空挡后，将近战敌人引至身旁，然后让远程的敌人AOE溅至其友军身上。 [*]这种诱敌往往是通过我们在主城[b]酒馆[/b]招募炮灰后可更加自如地实施，尤其对于远程流派（阿莓，看板娘）而言，炮灰成为吸引仇恨的火车王可太必要了。 [*]游戏更鼓励[b]让怪物产生位移的地形杀[/b]（用这种方式击杀，会获得名为“诸神认可”的局外进度点），这也正是暗合了游戏原名，[b]因为怪物不会在玩家回合自行移动，我们通过合理的技能释放，将其进行变位，从而直接使其即死[/b]。 [*]游戏允许一次关卡的随机重开，并且对于不会影响战局的移动，是可以撤回的[b]，这一点对我而言可能容错偏小，因为时常会将移动误点为推击[/b]，若是能直接撤回一回合，感觉就不会有太多的高压脑溢血时刻了。 [/list] [h2] [b]云海漫游：一场充满算计的肉鸽之旅[/b][/h2] 大地图探索仰赖空艇燃油，但鼓励贪婪，因为燃油耗尽无非是随机漂流，而且这对于驱散战争迷雾的开图反而更有裨益。辎重的临时燃油、回血道具、武器等，为探索以及战斗带来了更多助益。 除了浮空战，玩家可以在有限的疲劳值（如果不调减，积满疲劳就会强制重开）下前往事件岛，利用飞艇左侧的三维，合理的卖出属性，将每一次奇遇便为战力飞涨的契机。 但是就目前感受而言，游戏最重要的还得是货币，主城的市场、铁匠铺、迷雾开图、酒馆休憩与招募，都需要硬通货。因此，战斗远比事件重要。 因此能战则战，这对局内英雄升级以及局外双重的增益都有好处。 阿恩的狂战士越战越勇，阿莓的放风筝瞄准爆射等无不需要在局外的古神馈赠以及英雄轮回中取得终局强化后才能更加得心应手，[b]毕竟，这部游戏还是需要奖励擅于思考的战术家，防止他们不断碰壁。[/b] ……或者，新设污染，完成一定主线进度后带来新变量，将玩家置于新的利益天平，使之考虑是向死疯狂，还是小心翼翼地生存。 [quote]欢迎关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45531068/]黑白测评[/url] [hr]黑夜显真 白昼辨伪

I would NOT recommend my friends to play Dead Weight, however the game isn't bad-bad, so it's too punishing to leave a negative review. The game is a grind, not a challenge. It's a shame though, because the developers obviously spent a lot of time and effort on building the game. There are some simple ways to trivialize the game, like being able to generate infinite money while making the fatigue limit meaningless and acquiring infinite health on the starting hero. I played for 4 hours so for the price it's fine.

So positives first: Sound and music are pretty good. The pixel art of the backgrounds and character designs is great, but most of your time is spent in combat with a far less detailed version of your character. It is still decent, but not anywhere as good... The Game has two main mechanics: Exploration & Combat. The better of the two, Exploration, runs on Fuel, which limits reach and is refilled after combat. Which means to use it efficiently you always wanna go as far as possible before engaging in combat. You can also find little Events which offer minor decisions. The game also has a Fatigue system that allows you to engage with 9 Events or Combats before having to turn back to town to rest and reset, so you wanna leave some Combat Islands behind to guarantee your return trip. The map itself resets after you die or after you clear a chapter. You clear a chapter by finding and defeating a boss island. On my first chapter I cleared most islands while on my second one I found the boss after just half of my first fatigue bar. Since I cleared the combats on the way there and would have cleared the rest in the vicinity on my return trip, I had a choice to make: I could have turned around and come back later using Fuel Barrels, a resource purchasable in Town for these Situations, after looting and grinding the rest of the chapter map or I fight it immediately. Since the Combat was already annoying me at this point, for reasons I will get into, I chose the latter option. So far so okay. I am fine with it honestly, not a ton of depth, but serviceable. Now the Combat... Well, I guess the best thing one can call it is simple... If you consider that a good thing in a Tactics RPG, which I don't... The basic principle is that your enemies always go before you and wind-up their strikes, leaving you to react. Unfortunately your possible reactions are VERY limited. You have your main character which has an attack, movement and one special abilities plus any equipment you can get and equip. You can also hire different mercenaries who are the same, except no special ability and less equipment capacity plus lower base stats. Even after unlocking more characters it doesn't look like you can have more than one of them at a time... You can upgrade your character with different trees for VERY minor changes in how they behave during combat. Movement, attacks, equipment abilities and special abilities all draw from the same pool of action points, limiting your decisions further. Most turns in any fight basically come down to: hit the enemy and get out of their attack range, in either order. This leads to even simple fights being excessively drawn out and boring as you lack any more interesting responses and your enemy always maintains the initiative and dictates the pace of the fight. Combat damage is maintained between fights and healing resources are limited, especially if you don't wanna run back to town, which you can't afford to do anyway. Side note: It also repedeatly happened that I ran into a fight only for the random layout I spawned on and the first attacks to make it impossible to survive the first round no matter what I did. In that case your only option is to quit to the menu and load again, hoping you get a doable layout this time. Each chapter also introduces new game mechanics and those were what tipped the fights from boring into frustrating and extremely boring. All enemies in Chapter 2 get a self-buff that let's them immediately counter melee damage during your turn. It is important to mention here that the first main character you play as, the big huge barbarian warrior, starts with 3 max health and only has a melee attack by default... the first mercenary I got had 1 max health by default. And as I said healing between fights is limited... That buff has a 5 turn cooldown, which seems like you should just wait for them to use it and then attack them when it's down right? Well the buff also lasts those 5 rounds or until it activates... which essentially lead to melee attacks being functionally useless as a a strategy. The enemy health also doubled from the first chapter, while each of my warriors could still only reliably do one damage each turn... luckily, I had gotten ranged weapon equipment for both of them, meaning each fight turned into an annoying exercise of slowly widdeling the enemy health pool down and dodging out of the way... Oh, and remember how I mentioned unintentionally rushing the boss of chapter 2? Yeah, it wasn't a problem, I killed it without taking a single damage, while being way underleveled, it just took a while... And in Chapter 3 the special mechanic was another self-buff: every second turn the enemies could make it so their next strike would hit immediately on their turn instead of having wind-up, ignoring the main mechanic of this game's combat entirely... After the run, you get to unlock new abilities in a rogue-lite style system and that's probably what makes progression possible, but at that point I stopped caring. If you prefer to grind in order to beat a challenge, rather than figure out a character build or a working strategy to win, I'm sure you can have some fun with this game. Personally I don't consider this game to be a Tactics RPG at all, I consider it Dead Weight.

If you liked Enter the Breach, but want a casual and RPG experience, this is the game you're looking for. The gameplay can be repetitive and easy, but again, it's a casual experience that scratches the Enter the Breach itch. There is a top negative review that a lot of people seem to think is helpful and are probably steering them away from playing this game, but their review is based on a poor understanding of the game. I respect the way the developers responded to them, and that's the reason I decided to pull the trigger and buy the game. The following is what that bad review said about the game, and I'll tell you exactly why they are wrong: "Annoying mechanic #1: fuel. You burn fuel when moving between encounters, and when you inevitably run out of fuel, which always feels extremely premature, your run is over. There is apparently a gas station unlockable, but even after several hours of play, I never found it." Your run is not directly over when you run out of fuel. You have options, but not one of them leads to a direct game over. The game will prompt you to use consumables to either replenish your fuel or send you back to the home island. If you have nothing, you have the option to drift with reversable minor "negative" side effects. This option sends you to a random enemy island. From there, you just have to beat the enemy island to refuel. I actually use this mechanic to find new locations without burning through consumables and to grind EXP. Outside of these options, you can refill at the home island gas station, event islands, defeating wandering pirate ships, and defeating enemy islands. Fuel is not a direct game-ending issue. "Annoying mechanic #2: after ten encounters, your run is ended. Perhaps this is done for balance reasons, but it just feels annoying. Normally with rogue-lites your run is ended because you progressed to some combat that you couldn't win. But in Dead Weight, your run is ended just because you filled up this arbitrary progress bar." The game has an encounter bar of 10. Most events and enemy encounters cost 1, but I have found 1-2 events out of 50 that cost me 2. You can empty it with 20 gold on rare island events or you can pay 100 gold at the tavern in the main island. If you have a certain perk, every time you empty your encounter bar at a tavern your maximum encounter bar is increased by 1. I'm almost done with the game, and this encounter bar has not been an issue at all. Just do your resource management. "Annoying mechanic #3: the combat is akin to the Breach, which is fine, but it is more simplistic, and extremely repetitive. Due to Annoying Mechanics Numbers 1 & 2, everything is very slow to unlock, which adds further to the repetitiveness." If this reviewer followed my advice, they can unlock things faster because as they progress further into the game they get more post-game currency. Of course, if they're only playing 10 encounters per run, they're going to have a rough time. Once I understood I can replenish my encounter bar on my third run, I am progressing through the entire story mode. Now I spend a lot of time just grinding away amassing my strength to make the boss battles trivial. Now I will agree the game is repetitive because of this and due to the lack enemy and event variety. But if you want the scratch the casual EtB itch after a long day, this is the game. If the reviewer reads this, I hope they change their review. You're leading people away from a decent game.

I'm a little conflicted on this as I did have some fun. First of all, I don't really have a problem with the fuel or the fatigue systems, they do make clearing the whole stage more tedious in that you have to keep returning to the town to rest but it's just annoying not hard. You can run out of fuel fine and just keep going from another island. By a few islands in you can get enough money to buy fuel barrels and it's never an issue again. Upgrades do make this better but they're 'QoL' upgrades just to make it less tedious. My main problem is the combat is too easy and repetitive. Each character has a base set of skills and then can acquire more via items. They also have a set of skill trees that you can use to alter how they work, but they kind of always just play the same. The items can add some synergistic abilities but tend to be 'do damage in some way'. The armor and trinket items are a little better but are still just boring; Extra move, extra exp, extra health, survive 1 fatal blow, extra damage, extra wep slot, etc. The battles just tend to devolve into 'Move, Attack, End' over and over with little thought. And if you want to clear the whole screen in every act you are doing a whole ton of these battles that are over in 2-3 turns and have played out almost the exact same time every time. Maybe I should have been speed running to make the latter stagers harder because every time I get there I just completely stomp. The only unit losses I have are when I forget an enemy unit has retaliate. There are a couple mechanics to make the game harder. The first being the Madness mechanic that once sufficiently high replaces enemies with stronger versions and adds tentacles that block edges. However all this seemed to do for me is make the battles take longer and can be almost completely avoided via resetting madness with gold at the town. The other is when you complete a run you get a curse on future runs, but I cannot bring myself to continue unlocking these so I can't say much for them. Compared to the combat of Into the Breach there's just less of everything, nothing to defend so you never need to make sacrifices, less interactivity with battlefield manipulation or position mixing, encouraging pure dps over utility. No special terrains/hazards or battle effects, only 3 types of battle; Island, Ship and Boss. Also the events are all boring spend resource to gain thing or heal or refuel. Nothing unique or interesting, Multiple duplicates per act too so not a lot of variety. I really wanted to like this, and I was hoping for more advantage of the theme to be taken, like ship to ship combat and upgrades. Or more mission types like escorts, heists or bounties on unique pirate bosses. Instead it adds nothing new or exciting to the genre. It does look pretty though. Perhaps I'm being too harsh but It just felt like playing a game that wants to be an rpg with multiple heroes and skill trees but it didn't have enough content or story so it just became a subpar roguelite.

I enjoyed playing Dead Weight, but the game is held back by a number of questionable design decisions. In my opinion, the biggest of these issues is the inconsistency of the item reforging system. Some upgrades are straightforward improvements, while others completely change an item's role or even make it less useful than the previous tier. [u]For example, here are the stats for each stage of the Iron Swords:[/u] [b]Iron Sword (1 weapon slot, 1 skill):[/b] Sword Strike (1 damage, 1-2 range, 1 recovery) → [b]Bastard Sword (2 weapon slots, 2 skills):[/b] Sword Strike (3 damage, 1-2 range, 1 recovery) Double Strike (1 damage, 1-2 range, 2 recovery) → [b]Zwiehander (2 weapon slots, 1 skill):[/b] Sword Strike (5 damage, 1-2 range, 2 recovery) The Iron Sword begins as a cheap but weak weapon that can use Sword Strike every turn. Its first upgrade, the Bastard Sword, feels like a natural progression: Sword Strike is directly improved while the new Double Strike skill adds another tactical option. The weapon becomes stronger without losing what made it useful. The problem is the third tier. Rather than building on the Bastard Sword, the Zweihander removes Double Strike entirely and replaces the original Sword Strike with a stronger version that has a longer cooldown. Instead of feeling like a powerful late-game upgrade, it ends up being a side grade at best, despite potentially costing significantly more Obsession Crystals to obtain. Unfortunately, this issue crops up quite often. Several other weapons and mercenaries follow the same pattern, where their tier 3 upgrades feel weaker or less versatile than their tier 2 counterparts. I think many of these upgrades need to be reworked so they feel like genuine endgame improvements rather than trade-offs. I also noticed several other design quirks: [list]*Lumiere, a melee-only glass cannon, can be permanently cursed to make enemies explode on death, effectively making him unplayable.[/list] [list]*The main characters lose almost all story relevance after defeating the first boss.[/list] [list]*Enemies stop using traps after the first boss.[/list] [list]*Many encounters, including some boss fights, can be trivialized by pushing enemies off the map.[/list] There are also a number of bugs: [list]*Ranged weapons cannot attack across a one-tile-wide gorge.[/list] [list]*Enemies marked as immovable can still be pushed, dealing impact damage to adjacent characters.[/list] [list]*Enemies sometimes counterattack after being pushed away or falling.[/list] [list]*Some abilities do not function as described—for example, Silence sometimes fails to stop a boss's wind-up attack despite claiming to affect any enemy.[/list] Overall, I think Dead Weight is a fun game with a solid foundation, but I can't recommend it in its current state. None of these issues are individually game-breaking, but together add up and significantly hurt the overall experience. With some balance changes, bug fixes, and a rework of the tier 3 upgrade system, Dead Weight could become a game that I'd be happy to recommend.

[h1]就算是哥布林来了我也得给它推下去 [/h1] 作为独立工作室Klukva Games的第一款像素回合制战术游戏，不仅融合了蒸汽朋克与克苏鲁奇幻风格，而且还加入了飞船探索的肉鸽玩法，利用有限的油量，在漂浮空中的岛屿间来回穿梭，是要登岛战斗还是避其锋芒都由你来决定。 游戏一开始一位叫因西德的神对我进行了灵魂拷问，让我赶紧醒来直面那无法逃脱的命运，而当我睁开眼之后映入眼帘的却是三只不要命的哥布林，它们跳向我的船想要开始掠夺，结果有一只跳的太近直接飞下去了，这让我只能勉为其难打败另外两只了，解决之后我们搜刮了油箱，并向城中驶去。没想到降落的时候发现那里已经被真神女祭司所占领，并且哥布林也变成了浑身通红的颜色，危难之间我的挚友被抓走，而当我正想与他们大战一场的时候，却直接被抢先回合的哥布林推下去了，然后眼睛一闭又遇到了因西德，她叽里咕噜说了一堆又把我送回了物质世界，至此，新手教程结束，故事也就此展开。 要说本作最核心的亮点那就是通过地形来击退敌人，这也是区别于其他同类型游戏的战斗方式。由于我们是在空中飞行，所以每个战场也都是一座孤岛，利用敌人的移动位置和场上的一些木箱来进行规划，在它们靠边的时候直接推他们一把，从而进行秒杀。再搭配上不同职业的技能，还有不同的装备构筑，让每一次战斗都可以有不同的思路。并且我们所驾驶的飞船也是需要养成升级的，途中遇到其他飞船可以消耗炮弹数量直接进行摧毁，也可以选择登船与他们战斗，而我们行驶的时候油量会不断减少，如果油箱空了的话我们就只能选择消耗船身来增加油量或者随风而行，当你随风而行的时候就不一定会遇到什么了，这点就给整体游玩上增加了随机性。 我们每次战斗也会增加自身的疲劳值，上限为10点，如果快要满格了就需要回城里的酒馆花钱恢复，在城中也有着诸多建筑等待我们解锁升级，比如前期的灯塔，它的作用是可以照亮不同云层，方便你在行动时的路线选择，对它进行升级之后则可以去除更远范围的云雾，让途中的一切行动尽在掌握。而如果真要被哥布林拿下了其实也不用怕，因西德会把你再送回来的。 游戏在画面色彩与音效上也都做的很不错，无论是主角还是NPC的原画，乃至飞船船身上的细节都极为丰富，再搭配着富有史诗感的音乐，让作品完美的烘托出了在天空上当航空王的战斗快感。而且那克苏鲁大章鱼立在天空中时，也属实让我感觉压迫十足。 [h1]总结： [/h1] 本作凭借着地形战斗玩法以及独特的天空飞船探索设计，让一款战旗回合制游戏更加充满策略性。虽然有时候飞船航行战斗所带来的收益与付出不太成正比，但是好在游戏的核心玩法设计的不错。如果你是一个喜欢这种玩法并能接受一些奇幻元素的玩家，那么不妨来体验一下这款游戏。 [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]
